name: Set Covering Benchmark Dataset
description: This dataset contains 10,000 reproducible instances of the weighted Set Covering Problem, together with solver-certified integer and linear programming solutions, deterministic greedy solutions, rational certificates, and associated metadata. For the weighted Set Covering Problem, a collection of elements and a family of available subsets are given, with a positive (integer) cost assigned to each subset. The objective is to select subsets that cover every element while minimising total cost. The dataset is intended as a benchmark resource for computational experiments in combinatorial optimisation, integer programming, linear programming relaxations, approximation algorithms, greedy heuristics, and preprocessing. It may also be useful for algorithm benchmarking and teaching in operations research and computer science. The benchmark contains four matrix dimensions: (m, n) = (24, 40), (40, 70), (60, 100), and (100, 180), where m denotes the number of elements and n denotes the number of available subsets. Ten instance families are included: sparse random, medium-density random, dense random, block-structured, geometric disk-covering, interval-covering, redundant-column, dominated-column, community-structured, and planted-cover instances. Each family contains 1,000 instances, with 250 at each dimension, giving 10,000 instances in total.
